quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: In Hungarian, the word for butterfly is 'pillangó' (pronounced pee-lahn-go), which comes from a charming old folk belief that butterflies were attracted to flickering flames. The word relates to 'pillant' meaning 'glimpse' or 'flicker,' capturing how butterflies seem to dance through the air like little flames.

short_read.title: How Hummingbirds Navigate Thousands of Miles
short_read.teaser: These tiny birds, weighing less than a nickel, travel from Mexico to Alaska every year using an incredible internal compass. Scientists have discovered they can even remember every flower they've visited on their journey.

medium_read.title: The Gardens of Hungarian Castles Through the Centuries
medium_read.teaser: From medieval herb gardens to grand baroque landscapes, Hungary's historic estates showcase centuries of gardening traditions. Many of these beautiful gardens are being lovingly restored today, revealing forgotten plant varieties and design secrets.

long_read.title: The Secret Lives of Pacific Northwest Tide Pools
long_read.teaser: The rocky shores of the Olympic Peninsula host miniature worlds where sea stars, anemones, and tiny fish navigate the rhythm of the tides. This beautifully illustrated guide explores the fascinating creatures that make their homes between land and sea.

port_angeles.title: Black-Tailed Deer at Dusk
port_angeles.description: August evenings are perfect for spotting black-tailed deer at Olympic National Park's Heart O' the Hills area, just outside Port Angeles. These gentle deer are most active at dawn and dusk, often seen grazing in meadows with their fawns, who still have their spotted summer coats.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart beats approximately ___ times per minute during flight.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Wonderful! That's right — 1,200 beats per minute! That's about 20 times per second, which helps power their amazing hovering flight.
puzzle_1.close_response: Very close! A hummingbird's heart beats about 1,200 times per minute when flying — that's incredibly fast!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: A hummingbird's tiny heart actually beats about 1,200 times per minute during flight — that's one of the fastest heart rates in the animal kingdom!
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: To put this in perspective, a human heart beats about 60-100 times per minute at rest. Hummingbirds need this rapid heartbeat to fuel their energy-intensive hovering flight and incredibly fast wing beats.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Beautiful! Pillangó is indeed butterfly! The word has such a lovely, dancing sound, just like the creature itself.
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The Hungarian word for butterfly is 'pillangó' — such a musical word! (Madár means bird, virág means flower, and napraforgó means sunflower.)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is a unique language in Europe, part of the Finno-Ugric family rather than the Indo-European group. Its words often have poetic origins rooted in nature and folk traditions.

puzzle_3.question: What color are a flamingo's feathers when they are born?
puzzle_3.correct_response: That's right! Baby flamingos are born with gray or white feathers and only turn pink from eating algae and shrimp rich in carotenoids. It takes about two years for them to develop their signature pink color!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: Flamingo chicks are actually born with gray or white feathers! They gradually turn pink over about two years from eating algae and tiny shrimp that contain natural pink pigments called carotenoids.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: The pinker a flamingo is, the healthier it tends to be — bright pink coloring signals that the bird is eating well and is likely to be a more attractive mate. Some flamingos can even be orange or red depending on their diet!
